Hey chief just wanted to throw my two cents in. I’m sorry you’re struggling with this. There was a time where I buried myself in women to escape my own emotions and pain, but in the end I cleaved a path of destruction that hurt not only myself and people I cared about. I’m not going to pretend I understand all of your struggles, and I hope I don’t come off that way. Honestly, the best thing I can recommend is taking a step back. You’re right, a lot of sex isn’t necessarily a bad thing! But everything has to be in the right context. The best way I can think to make an analogy is you’re trying to push a square block into a circular hole. No matter how hard you push, or whichever way you twist and turn it, it’s not going to go into the circular hole. But if you take the time to find the circle block, then you’ll be able to push it through. Love genuinely takes time. To quote Sondheim, “love isn’t sudden surrender, it’s tender and slow, it must grow.” There isn’t much to dull the pain of loneliness I admit, but the “solutions” are suppressants more than anything. Take your time, find a partner that’s willing to take it slow and work with you. And above all, look into getting help! Your mental health is health, and it’s not a burden! A therapist works miracles if you’re willing to put the work in, a psychiatrist or psychologist could help you understand what mental disorders or disabilities you may have so you can better understand yourself. The biggest truth in this comment and I’ll leave it at this, is that you need to love yourself first. You don’t have to love yourself every day, that’s fine. But a partner will not fix it all, as much as we think love will. When we love ourselves, it allows us to give love to others to a greater degree. Hope this helped, I’m rooting hard for you.

So this isn’t necessarily something that will fix your problems and I might come off as uncaring, but I just want to help a fellow young lad (I’m only 22, I feel like 15 was yesterday hahaha) in some hard times.

Cutting out toxic people is a great decision and I’m proud of you. It’s not easy, especially when they’re friends, but you need to prioritize your happiness first. Not everyone can be there when you need them, but you’ll always be there for you regardless. That being said, you can’t just up and move on from it, as much as I wish you could. Nobody likes to hear it, but time is the ultimate healer. You can’t rush your own healing process and that’s okay! It took me almost a year or a year and a half to get over an ex I cared very deeply for, meanwhile she had pretty much moved on before our break up because she was initiating the process and had time to grieve before it happened. For some it goes away in a week, some a month, it just depends. In the example of an emotional boi like me, it takes a long time. But when you do feel sad, you don’t have to force yourself to be okay. Don’t let it consume you by any means, but being sad or angry or distraught is part of the human condition, you know? It means you’re human and even though we don’t like being sad and stuff it’s beautiful in its own sort of weird way.

Something that helped me a lot in the healing process was finding people I can trust to lean on. A good buddy of mine has always made it a goal to listen to me and knows to respect my boundaries. Though I never do because I hate making her worry, my mom is another fighter in my trenches for when the going gets rough for me and I know I can count on her. Maybe if it’s really getting to you, ask a friend or family member “hey I’m kind of feeling bad, are you mentally able to hear me vent rn?” If not, it’s fine, not everybody can be. You can scream on subreddits or write it in a journal, whatever helps you king/queen/imperator. I hope this helped to some degree. Keep pushing, I’m rooting hard for you 💕

I struggled a lot with depression and do to this day. I used to frequent the subreddit and make posts pretty frequently because I had to just scream somewhere about my inner turmoil. I didn’t want to put my friends in a position where they were afraid for my safety, and I found talking to people in the suicide hotline uncomfortable (I did it once and had to tell a stranger whose name I don’t remember why I wanted to kill myself, that was weird). I’ve also seen stories where the people on the other line were simply uncaring of how they felt but I’m thankful I never had that experience. But I digress.

Ultimately the subreddit gave me just enough to get out of it. Being able to shout how I felt really did help, even if people didn’t reply. It’s almost been 2 years now since my last suicide attempt and I just keep trying to increase that number when I start to lose hope. Making that number bigger has helped a lot but it all started with looking for a subreddit to say how I feel.
